Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2971); Jairus (i.e. Jair), an Israelite:--Jairus.
BiblicalUsage: Jairus was a ruler of the synagogue, a man with standing, and he threw it all aside to fall at Jesus' feet for his dying daughter. In Mark 5:22 he comes and falls at his feet and begs him greatly, and in Luke 8:41 the same scene is told again, a father pleading for his only daughter, about twelve years old.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jairus shows what real faith looks like when it has run out of options: a respected man on his knees, asking Jesus for the one thing nobody else could give.
